answers.answer: WTI daily nominal spot quote at Cushing, Oklahoma: minus $36.98 per barrel. Separate from minus $37.63 May WTI futures settlement.
20 April 2020, minus $36.98, one observed trading day; Friday 17 April $18.31 and Tuesday 21 April $8.91. Thus a $55.29 fall from Friday.

Prose attributes it to lockdown demand collapse, filling Cushing storage, low liquidity and imminent expiry of physically delivered May WTI futures on 21 April. No independent causal test supplied by charts.

Seller pays someone to accept oil; in the futures account a trader unable to take delivery pays another party to take the contract and obligation. Connection between the futures transaction and spot quote remains incompletely explained.
WTI went negative while Brent stayed positive. Cannot establish worldwide exclusivity from two benchmarks. Both experienced the broader price collapse.

WTI returned positive the next day; both benchmarks recovered toward $40 by June. Prose does not explain the sustained subsequent recovery; expiry timing helps suggest why the immediate squeeze was temporary.

Charts establish benchmark prices, timing, relative paths and positive weekly/monthly averages. Prose adds historical uniqueness and attributed causal explanation. Data alone cannot prove causation, storage conditions, actual individual contract payments, or worldwide scope.
